title: The AI Committee Is Step Two Now, Not the Last Gate
summary: Jean-Marc Chanoine went from Navy JAG defense attorney to Accenture procurement consultant to Chief Sales Officer at Templafy, which he joined as a strategic AE in 2019 after cold-emailing the CEO. In this episode he argues that selling AI into the enterprise has become a political problem rather than a technical one, because executives who got burned by early AI investments now optimize for the safe bet over the best bet. He breaks down how he handles buyers who stall out believing they can build it themselves, why the AI committee has to be engaged in the second step of the cycle instead of the last, and why organizations consistently overestimate how well they understand their own processes. Worth a listen for anyone selling software into large enterprises where the buying committee is deciding with their careers, not just their budgets.
keyQuote: If you don't have that early engagement with the folks that run the AI strategy, you're going to end up getting shot at the end of the sale cycle. It's not the last step; it's almost the second step.
guestTitle: Chief Sales Officer and GM of the Americas, Templafy
guestBio: Jean-Marc Chanoine is Chief Sales Officer and GM of the Americas at Templafy, the document generation platform that helps roughly four million users eliminate manual document work. He spent five years as a lawyer in the US Navy JAG Corps, then earned an MBA at Berkeley and joined Accenture Strategy as a senior strategy consultant working on procurement and process transformation. A document automation project there burned four or five million dollars with an unnamed hyperscaler and failed, which sent him looking for software that could compile contracts; a Google search turned up Templafy. He emailed the CEO asking for a job, was asked whether he could sell, said yes without ever having sold anything, and joined the New York office in February 2019 to build the strategic accounts function aimed at the Big Four. Seven and a half years later he runs sales for the Americas and writes for the Forbes Business Development Council.
takeaways: The AI committee is step two in the cycle now, not the last gate.
Nobody gets fired for buying the biggest name in AI.
Frontier models give the software away and charge for the tokens.
Don't argue with build-it-ourselves. Hand over the docs and wait.
95% of the time the build attempt is a delay, not a lost deal.
Buyers overestimate how well they know their own processes.
Your top 1% rep is still your top 1% rep. AI lifts the floor.
